title: Clarify P1/P2 English fallback coverage in multilingual entry pages

sources.reason: English reader entry and current coverage warning.
Chinese reader entry and current coverage warning.
Japanese reader entry and current coverage warning.
Canonical P0/P1/P2 localization policy and topic examples.
Authoritative current P1/P2 route inventory; read-only source.
Existing navigation and fallback-policy regression coverage.

rawUserRequest: Make the statement that some P1/P2 technical references remain English-only correspond explicitly to the multilingual entry pages, while preserving the truthful boundary that full multilingual coverage is not complete. Continue through the complete Work Item lifecycle.

declaredIntent.summary: Make the current P1/P2 English fallback state directly understandable from every language entry page without requiring a maintainer to infer it from the registry.

riskAssessment.reason: The entry-page wording must name the current English-only P1/P2 references without implying that P1/P2 translation is universally required or that coverage is complete.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: The scope, source inventory, acceptance, and verification are explicit; no human decision is required to make the bounded wording change.

preReviewWarnings: Review that each language names the same current P1/P2 English-only facts and preserves the non-completion boundary.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese documentation entry pages explicitly state that active P1 command/schema references currently use English-only canonical routes and that the active P2 documentation-authority reference is not translated by default.
All three entry pages state that these fallback policies must not be interpreted as complete multilingual coverage, and link readers to the canonical documentation architecture policy.
The wording remains semantically aligned across languages and does not change the registry, validator, P0 topic status, or technical reference content.
Focused documentation journey tests and all Contract lifecycle checks pass, including a regression assertion that the three entry pages retain the fallback boundary.
guidelines: Name the current P1/P2 English-only facts explicitly; do not rely on a generic migration disclaimer.
Keep English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese semantics equivalent while allowing natural language differences.
Do not imply that P1/P2 English fallback is complete multilingual coverage or that every P1/P2 page must be translated.
Do not modify the authoritative registry or validator in this entry-page clarification Work Item.

intent.problem: The current entry pages warn generally that incomplete routes are not evidence of complete multilingual coverage, but they do not tell readers which active P1/P2 technical references are English-only today. Nontechnical readers should not need to infer the limitation from a maintainer registry.
constraints: Keep the change limited to reader-facing entry and policy prose plus focused tests.
Preserve the existing P0 multilingual journey and the registry's machine-readable policy.
Do not translate or rewrite the P1/P2 technical reference pages in this Work Item.
intent.rationale: A direct, three-language statement makes the current documentation boundary legible at the point of entry and prevents an overclaim without creating an unnecessary translation obligation.
